# Session record — v1.7.0 white-label, Phase 0

**Date:** 2026-08-27 · **Model:** Claude Opus 5 · **Branch:** `main`

Context for whoever picks this up. The decisions below were made with the user
in conversation; several reversed an earlier position after measurement, and the
reasoning matters more than the outcome. The plan itself is
[`v1.7-white-label-plan.md`](v1.7-white-label-plan.md); this file records how it
was arrived at.

---

## What happened, in order

### 1. Released 1.6.5 (commit `8724697`)

Unrelated to white-label but it is the base this work sits on. Thirteen screens
reported filter, search and dropdown controls as "transparent to background".
One cause, not thirteen: `Input`, `Textarea` and `SelectTrigger` in
`packages/frontend/src/components/ui/` all shipped `bg-transparent`, so every one
painted whatever sat behind it. Fixed at the three primitives (now
`bg-background`), and two redundant call-site overrides were removed so the fill
is declared in exactly one place. Standard written up under "Form Control Fill"
in `packages/frontend/docs/styling/README.md`; root cause in `ISSUES.md` #79.

Worth knowing: the user's reported OKLCH samples did **not** match
`bg-background`. They pointed at two in-project reference controls instead, and
those were treated as authoritative. Recorded in ISSUES.md #79.

### 2. Researched LOTTO and ZEV Prism

The document the user first linked —
`~/Repos/lotto/docs/WHITE_LABEL_BRANDING_PLAN.md` — is **not** the port target.
It describes build-time, code-owned brand profiles selected by an environment
variable (LOTTO v1.19.0). The Appearance wizard lives in the second layer,
`~/Repos/lotto/docs/CONFIGURABLE_BRANDING_PLAN.md` (LOTTO v1.20.0). Read that
one.

FEED already owns the UX idiom: LOTTO built its Appearance stepper on the
pattern it inherited *from* FEED's AI Configuration wizard. That component is
`packages/frontend/src/components/ai-configuration/shared/BaseAIConfigDialog.tsx`
and it is what Phase 2 must build on. Workflow parity is the acceptance
criterion — a staff member who has branded LOTTO must not have to relearn
anything.

ZEV Prism's `~/Repos/zev_app/zev_dashboard/docs/semantic-settings.md` is the
model for Phase 4 terminology.

### 3. Three architectural divergences found

These are why the v1.6→v2.0 roadmap's description of this work as "Mechanical"
was pushed back on. The design ports; the delivery is a rewrite.

1. **FEED authors tokens as bare HSL triplets, LOTTO is OKLCH-native.** 118
   tokens in `packages/frontend/src/index.css` consumed as `hsl(var(--token))`
   — and, critically, as `hsl(var(--background) / 0.40)` in the app-shell
   atmosphere, which reads the raw triplet. A derived `oklch()` cannot be
   substituted. Hence: derive structurally, serialize to HSL now, swap the
   serializer at v1.7.5.
2. **No SSR.** LOTTO injects theme CSS into its Next.js layout.
   `packages/frontend/index.html` is a static build artifact served by nginx
   (`docker/nginx.conf`, `try_files`). The replacement is *simpler*: one
   render-blocking `<link rel="stylesheet">` to a backend route.
3. **No PWA manifest in FEED**, so LOTTO's manifest/install-identity work has no
   counterpart. But FEED has PDFs, CSVs and branded email, which LOTTO does not.

### 4. Decisions taken with the user

Eleven decisions, all settled, recorded in the plan's "Decisions and reasoning"
table. The ones that shaped the code:

- **Snap to Tailwind v4 rather than reproduce brand colours exactly.** The user
  overruled an initial recommendation to keep the brand hue exact. Their
  argument: brand alignment is reconstructing a colour *story*, not matching a
  hex; perception does not track the maths closely enough for exactness to pay
  for itself. They were right, and the initial carve-out was also inconsistent
  with the chart recommendation already accepted ("rank, don't generate").
- **Charts rank IBM Carbon, never generate.** Preserves an existing
  WCAG-verified palette.
- **Protected families absent from the schema**, not merely discouraged.
- **Assets in the database** (LOTTO's are filesystem-backed and not durable on
  Vercel; FEED has no such constraint and gains backup portability).
- **v1.7.0 ships at Phase 2, v1.7.1 after Phase 4, v1.7.5 for OKLCH.**

### 5. Phase 0 built (commits `f222b05`, `d12bd5f`)

Six findings the tests forced, each of which changed the design:

| Finding | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Role-aware pooling is **not** enough to keep a dead-neutral charcoal off a tinted family — `olive-800` is genuinely nearest even within the neutral pool | `CHROMA_WEIGHT = 3` in `snap.ts` |
| A brand can need a different accent per theme — FEED's light primary is WTH blue, its dark primary is WTH gold | `BrandInput.accentDark` |
| `border` must not be held to the 3:1 UI floor; WCAG 1.4.11 exempts decorative container edges and FEED ships 1.55:1 | `kind: 'decorative'`, floor 1.3 |
| `yellow-600` is 2.94:1 on white — the only failure across all 153 themes | `ring` light stop moved 600 → 700 for every family |
| `CARBON_CATEGORICAL_ORDER` already hops the colour wheel for colour-vision deficiency; re-ranking would destroy it | `charts.ts` **rotates** rather than sorts |
| The sidebar has its own token family and did not rebrand — caught in the browser, invisible to unit tests | Eight `sidebar-*` tokens added |

**A claim in the plan doc was wrong and was corrected.** An earlier draft said
role-aware pooling moves St. Johns' charcoal to `zinc-800`. It does not; chroma
weighting is what does. The committed plan carries the corrected version.

### 6. Stop-map review with the user

The user reviewed all 25 tokens as swatch pairs (current FEED vs derived, both
themes) and raised three calls:

1. **The dark accent surface went brown.** `--accent` took stop 800 from the
   primary's family; WTH gold resolved to `amber-800` = `#973c00` across every
   dark hover and selected surface. Measurement showed this is *not* chroma
   loss — amber keeps 73% of its chroma from 500 to 800 — it is that `amber-800`
   sits at hue 46, lightness 47%, and dark orange is brown. No stop inside the
   warm band escapes it.
2. **`secondary` and `muted` collapsed** to byte-identical values.
3. **Is `accent` a brand colour at all?** The user's answer introduced the
   ranking idea below.

The user's framing on (3) drove the fix for (1): a brand is an ordered set, not
one colour — Coke is red then white; Pepsi is red, blue, then a black-and-white
split; Google runs four chromatics over neutrals; IBM is one blue. WTH's logo
reads blue → teal → gold. Once ranked, the accent surface takes the **second**
colour, so dark `--accent` became `#005f5a` (deep teal) and the divergence from
what FEED ships disappeared entirely.

LOTTO already implements exactly this (`~/Repos/lotto/src/lib/brand-theme/color-story.ts`
plus `~/Repos/lotto/src/components/appearance/palette-extract.ts`): median-cut
extraction from the logo, ranked by pixel population weighted by chroma salience
so a small saturated mark beats a large pale wash. FEED's `color-story.ts`
mirrors its role model.

### 7. One instruction not followed as given

The user said muted elements can sacrifice contrast — "losing contrast in that
context is a feature". The principle was accepted; the palette will not deliver
it. Measured across all 153 themes, `muted-foreground` at 600/400 clears at 6.26
and 5.56; the next step down (600/500) drops dark muted text to 3.03:1, and
there is no stop between. `text-muted-foreground` carries real body copy in FEED
(card descriptions, table detail, footnotes) and WCAG 1.4.3 has no exemption for
text meant to be quiet. Left at the passing pair with the measurement recorded
at the call site in `tokens.ts`. **This was flagged back to the user as a
deliberate departure for them to make explicitly if they still want it.**

### 8. Eighteen tokens flagged for later review

Recorded in `packages/backend/src/services/brand-theme/review-list.ts`, guarded
by `__tests__/stop-map-review.test.ts`. Two were resolved the same day by the
accent-rank change. These are not failures — everything clears its floor — they
are where the derived value moved further from the hand-tuned original than the
user expected, worth re-judging in the browser once the wizard exists.

## Out-of-scope findings raised

- **FEED's dark focus ring is 1.50:1**, below the WCAG 1.4.11 floor for focus
  indicators. `--ring`, `--sidebar-primary` and `--sidebar-ring` in dark all
  carry the identical value `222 10.9% 18%`, which is the signature of copied
  placeholders. The derived themes clear 3:1, so this is on the accepted-
  divergence list rather than inherited. A separate task was flagged for it.
- **`packages/frontend/src/test/chart-colors.test.ts` will go stale.** It reads
  `--card` out of `index.css` and asserts 4.5:1 against it. Once surfaces become
  configurable it keeps passing against the compiled default while a real
  agency's saved surface could push chart series below the floor. Phase 0's
  `contrast-proof.test.ts` supersedes it; delete or rewrite the frontend one
  when Phase 1 lands.
- **AGENTS.md paths are stale.** It says the active repo is
  `/Users/russbook/williamtemple-feed`; the live checkout is
  `/Users/russbook/Repos/williamtemple-feed`. Three places repeat the old path.

- Browser, on the user's own dev server at `localhost:5173`: derived themes for
